title: Factors in Deciding Whether or Not to Press Charges Against Persons with Disabilities
what_it_is: Factors in Deciding Whether or Not to Press Charges Against Persons with Disabilities

sections.label: Public Prosecutor charging considerations
sections.summary: The Public Prosecutor considers facts, evidence, public interest and any mental condition, and may issue a warning instead of charging.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In deciding whether to charge a person, the Public Prosecutor will consider the facts, the sufficiency of evidence and the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Where the person has a mental condition or disability, the Public Prosecutor will consider the nature of the mental condition or disability, its severity and the connection, if any, between the mental condition or disability and the alleged offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Where appropriate, for example, where the person has no criminal history, the alleged offence is not serious and the person's culpability is lowered as a result of his mental condition or disability, the Public Prosecutor may decide to issue a warning, instead of charging the person.

sections.label: Prosecution charge and treatment order
sections.summary: The Prosecution charged the offender as the offences were not minor, but sought a mandatory treatment order given his mental condition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Prosecution decided to charge him, considering that the offences were not minor.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: However, taking into account his mental condition, the Prosecution submitted for a mandatory treatment order to be imposed against the offender, which required the offender to undergo psychiatric treatment in lieu of imprisonment or a fine.

sections.label: Appropriate Adult Scheme interviews
sections.summary: The AAPMD, introduced in 2015 and run by MINDS, provides trained Appropriate Adults to support persons with mental or intellectual disabilities during law enforcement interviews.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Specifically, the Member may be aware of the Appropriate Adult Scheme for Persons with Mental Disabilities (AAPMD) which was introduced in 2015 to support persons with mental or intellectual disabilities during law enforcement interviews.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: AAPMD is administered by the Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore (MINDS).

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Under this scheme, an Appropriate Adult who is a trained volunteer is present during interviews to facilitate communications between the IO and the person with mental or intellectual disability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The Appropriate Adult watches for signs of distress, supports the emotional well-being of the person and assists in communication.
